scope: Complete source-bound Śrīdhara commentary for Canto 11 Chapter 1, verses 11.1.8–11.1.10.

entries.sanskrit: अब्रह्मण्येभ्योऽदातृभ्यो वाऽसेवकेभ्यो वा विप्राः कुप्यन्ति, वृष्णयस् तु न तथेत्य् आह---ब्रह्मण्यानाम् इत्य्-आदिना । किं च, कोपे जातेऽपि कृष्ण-चेतसां कथम् अभूत्? कथं प्रादुरभूद् इत्य् अर्थः ॥८॥
word_for_word: at those not devoted to brahmins
or at those who do not give
or at those who do not serve
beginning with the word ‘devoted to brahmins’
of those whose minds are on Kṛṣṇa
how did it come to be?
entries.literal_english: Brahmins become angry with people who disregard brahmins, do not give, or fail to serve; the Vṛṣṇis were not like those people. That is why the verse begins ‘of those devoted to brahmins.’ Moreover, even supposing anger arose, how could [a curse] come to pass against those whose minds were fixed upon Kṛṣṇa? ‘How did it occur?’ means ‘how did it arise?’
entries.note: The question whether the curse could take effect is Śrīdhara's own further question; no alternative interpretation from Jīva is inserted.

entries.sanskrit: अतः स्पष्टस्य निमित्तस्य भवान् निमित्तान्तरं पृच्छति---यन्-निमित्त इति । एकात्मनाम् एक-चित्तानां कथं भेदः कलहः ? ॥९॥
word_for_word: in the words beginning ‘because of what cause?’
entries.literal_english: Since the apparent cause is already evident, you ask about another cause with the words beginning ‘because of what cause?’ How could there be dissension, that is, quarrel, among those who are of one mind?
entries.note: Śrīdhara specifically glosses ekātmanām as ‘of one mind’; a different gloss in the Jīva section is not attributed to him.

entries.sanskrit: ईश्वरेच्छैवात्र निमित्तम् इति परिहरति---बिभ्रद् इति । सकलानां सुन्दर-वस्तूनां सन्निवेशो विन्यास-विशेषो यस्मिंस् तद् वपुर् बिभ्रत् । तर्हि किम् अतिसौन्दर्याद् विषय-परः ? न, सु-मङ्गलं कर्माचरन् । तत् किं, कयापि कामनया ? न, आप्त-कामः । तर्हि किम् इति कर्माचरति ? धाम द्वारवत्य्-अख्यं गृहम् आस्थाय रममाणः गृहे रममाणान् कर्म ग्राहयितुम् इत्य् अर्थः । ननु, किम् आप्त-कामस्य गृह-रत्या कर्मभिर् वा ? तत्राह---उदार-कीर्तिः उदारा बहु-फल-प्रदा कीर्तिर् यस्य सः, कीर्ति-वितानार्थम् इत्य् अर्थः । एवं परमैश्वर्येण वर्तमान एव कुलं संहर्तुम् ऐच्छत् । तत् कस्य हेतोः ? स्थितः कृत्ये भू-भार-हरणे शेषो यस्य सः ॥१०॥
word_for_word: no, since his desires are fulfilled
why then does he perform acts?
what need has one whose desires are fulfilled
for domestic enjoyment or for acts?
for the expansion of his glory
entries.literal_english: The cause is the Lord's will alone; the answer begins with ‘bearing.’ He bore a form in which the beauty of all beautiful things was arranged in a special way. Was he then attached to sense objects because of that surpassing beauty? No: he performed wholly auspicious acts. Did he do so from desire? No: his desires were fulfilled. Why perform action, then? He dwelt and took pleasure in the home called Dvāravatī to induce those who enjoy household life to undertake actions. But why would one of fulfilled desires need domestic pleasure or actions? The verse replies that he had generous fame—fame bestowing many fruits—and acted to spread it. Even while possessing supreme sovereignty, he wished to withdraw his dynasty. Why? The removal of the earth's burden remained among his tasks.
entries.note: Śrīdhara's sequence of objection and response is preserved. The separate Jīva reading of the Lord's remaining pastime is not substituted.
